subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Gartner Duct Cyst and Imperforate Hymen

steps.tx: A cyst of the mesonephric duct remnant in the anterolateral vaginal wall is a **Gartner duct cyst**. Most are small, silent and found incidentally. Large ones distort the urethra and associate with ipsilateral renal anomalies. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Gartner duct cysts sit in the anterolateral vaginal wall from mesonephric remnants.

steps.tx: Fusion of the hymen without perforation trapping menstrual blood at puberty is an **imperforate hymen**. Cyclic pain, primary amenorrhoea and a bulging bluish membrane diagnose it. Cruciate incision drains haematocolpos completely. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Imperforate hymen traps menstrual blood behind a bulging bluish membrane.

steps.tx: Distinguishing Gartner cyst from Bartholin cyst depends on position, anterolateral high versus posterolateral low, termed **cyst localisation**. Skene duct cysts sit near the urethral meatus instead. Excision is reserved for symptomatic lesions. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Cyst localisation separates high anterolateral Gartner from low posterolateral Bartholin cysts.

steps.tx: Blood collected in the vagina behind an obstruction is **haematocolpos**. It can reach a litre and compress bladder causing retention. Ultrasound shows the fluid level and the obstructing membrane or septum. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Haematocolpos collects blood in the vagina and can cause urinary retention.

steps.tx: Further accumulation into uterus and tubes gives haematometra and haematosalpinx as **ascending collections**. Retrograde spill may seed endometriosis in delayed cases. Early drainage prevents these sequelae entirely. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Ascending collections fill uterus and tubes when haematocolpos is neglected.

steps.tx: Ectopic ureter opening into a Gartner cyst causes continuous dribbling incontinence in girls, a classic **ectopic ureter association**. Normal voiding continues alongside the constant leak. Imaging finds the duplicated system responsible. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Ectopic ureter into a Gartner cyst causes continuous dribbling with normal voiding.

steps.tx: Surgery for imperforate hymen excises a disc of membrane rather than simple puncture, following **cruciate excision** technique. Simple puncture reseals and risks ascending infection. The excised edge is marsupialised to stay open. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Cruciate excision marsupialises the hymen edge because simple puncture reseals.

steps.tx: Never aspirate a presumed haematocolpos blindly because a septum or cervix may intervene, a **no blind aspiration** rule. Examination under anaesthesia with ultrasound guidance defines anatomy first. Wrong level surgery creates strictures. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: No blind aspiration of haematocolpos because septum level must be defined first.

steps.tx: After drainage, patency is checked at follow up and fertility prognosis is excellent, termed **post drainage review**. Adhesion of the incised membrane is the main early complication. Most girls menstruate normally thereafter. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Post drainage review checks patency, and fertility prognosis is excellent.
